summary: Cold-read plan-gate grill (gpt-5.6-sol @ high, launch-ea82a7d8acae43c2aab7f572df2bf68c) interrogated docs/local-dev-full-plan-draft.md against the roadmap acceptance criteria, the active decision corpus, and docs/architecture/. It raised four owner decisions (reset-db recovery/marker semantics, decision 0006 host/port precedent, decision 0001 CLI-persistence boundary, and one-task-vs-split sizing) plus eleven repository-answerable amendments (circular preflight ordering, home-bootstrap-before-checks separation, storage/auth reading the same revision, the ownership-marker 'never'-vs-'rewritten' contradiction, TTY reachability without touching auth.ts, ownedPostgres endpoint verification, pg_stat_activity wording precision, a stale roadmap criterion, user_facing/functional-check misclassification, a missing README acceptance criterion, a wrong verify-script path plus missing verification cases, a non-deterministic manual crash test, and a wrong decision citation/toolchain-justification gap). The owner chose all four recommended options; every other finding was resolved directly in the amended plan.
gaps: reset-db drops the settings_revisions table it just treated as authoritative, and every command refuses a stale reset marker while the remediation says to rerun the same command -- an endless refusal loop.

The plan writes GANTRY_CONTROL_HOST and GANTRY_CONTROL_PORT into .env, but decision 0006 reserves environment values for runtime-owned secrets and places non-secret configuration in settings revisions; no existing bind-host/port exception covered this.

Decision 0001 says CLI adapters must not directly mutate persistence, while the plan kept schema reset, revision reads, and pg_stat_activity queries inside local.ts with only a spawn exception named, and local.ts was already close to the 700-line architecture ceiling.
The current staged change is already 1,646 additions across eight files before the remaining safety work, and the sole task covers roughly twenty distinct proof seams.

The preflight contract read as circular: container start must follow authority validation, but authority validation requires Postgres, with no stated reversible-exception/restore-prior-state handling.
localEnvironment creates the home and writes .env before authority checks, with no stated separation between additive bootstrap and destructive/mutating preconditions.

Storage and authentication authority were checked from different sources (storage from the settings revision, authentication from YAML) instead of the same authoritative revision with the min_reader_version fence.
The ownership marker lifecycle read as self-contradictory: 'bootstrap only, never later' versus 'rewritten by full reset', with no reconciling rule.
The settled TTY rule appeared to require adding apps/core/src/cli/auth.ts to write scope, since gantry ui authorize as a spawned subprocess always prints the raw URL unconditionally.
ownedPostgres verifies mount and checkout identity, not the promised published host/port endpoint, so host/port binding verification was missing.
pg_stat_activity detects any active database client, not specifically an orphaned core process, and the spec/plan wording did not say so.
The roadmap's session/link acceptance criterion is stale against the settled non-TTY and mandatory-attempt/fail-open semantics.
The root decomposition's user_facing flag and functional-check requirement did not reflect that the acceptance path includes a real browser-session redemption, even though no React component changed.
README/build documentation lacked a stated acceptance criterion, repeating the active plan-contract-partial recurring finding class.

The Verify Plan named a nonexistent .agents/scripts/verify.py path, omitted format:check:web, real-Postgres authority/orphan verification cases, and package-script routing proof and build-artifact-parity checks; the manual crash test was timing-dependent and could collide with an existing runtime home; and the Decisions section cited decision 0143 instead of 0132 for authorization-token governance with no toolchain-choice justification stated.
resolutions: Owner chose 'Preserve desired state': before the destructive schema step, write the validated authoritative revision out as settings.yaml (a matching recovery copy); a separate, later requirements re-grill further resolved the marker refusal loop with an explicit --after-manual-recovery operator-acknowledgment flag, now stated in the plan's Technical Approach and Acceptance Criteria and in the amended spec.

Owner chose 'Record a narrow decision amendment': docs/decisions/0162-local-bootstrap-host-port-env-exception.md (accepted), scoping the exception to exactly GANTRY_CONTROL_HOST/GANTRY_CONTROL_PORT for the bootstrap moment before any settings source is reachable, later amended further to state process-env precedence for these same two keys.

Owner chose 'Record a bounded local-operator deviation and allow one suffixed repository file': apps/core/src/cli/local-postgres.ts now holds ownedPostgres, the latest-settings-revision read, and the pg_stat_activity check, documented as local-operator-only and never imported by agent/tool/job code; added to write scope and size budget.

Owner chose to keep one task with an explicit size budget rather than split: Task Decomposition now states a 2,000-added-line target ceiling across the product-code/test write scope, a 2x (4,000-line) ceiling before stage-done's hard refusal, and NOTE-not-refusal treatment in between.

Plan now states the reversible bootstrap-then-check start is itself part of the check, not a mutation it must follow; on a failed check only a container this invocation itself started is stopped, never an already-running one.

Plan now separates additive fresh-home bootstrap (home directory, .env, marker, container/volume creation) from destructive/mutating preconditioned steps; additive steps may precede authority checks and are safe to leave in place if a check later fails.

Plan now requires storage and authentication authority to be read from the SAME authoritative revision object, using the canonical revision parser and min_reader_version skew rejection normal startup already enforces.

Plan now states a full reset rewrites the ownership marker only on a home that already carried one (re-affirming existing ownership), never on a home with no marker (refused exactly like filesystem reset) -- reconciling 'never after bootstrap' with 'rewritten by full reset'.

Plan now requires the in-process authorization-issuance path (the same function gantry ui authorize uses) rather than inheriting a spawned subprocess's stdio, so the TTY gate applies without adding apps/core/src/cli/auth.ts to write scope.
Plan now extends the ownedPostgres check to verify the container's actual published host/port binding matches the endpoint being reset, not just mount/checkout identity.
Plan and spec now state the active-connection check detects any active database client, which includes but is not limited to an orphaned core process.
Plan now includes updating the stale roadmap session/link criterion (and other stale doc mentions of the removed CLI surface) in its Technical Approach and CLI-surface-reduction bullet.

Plan now records the task's user_facing flag as true (root decomposition), requiring the functional-checker to walk the start-to-browser-session path and the implementer to attest emil-design-eng/frontend-design as reviewed-with-no-visual-changes.
Plan now adds an explicit README acceptance criterion documenting the full build-command set and dropping obsolete explicit-only authorization guidance.

Plan's Verify Plan now uses the correct factory/scripts/verify.py path, adds format:check:web, package-script routing proof, and a falsifiable dist/ build-equivalence check; Manual Verification adds real-Postgres schema-conflict/orphan-core/orphan-Vite cases and a deterministic crash test using a repo-built CLI against a freshly created temporary parent; the Decisions section now cites 0132 (not 0143) for authorization-token governance and states the reused-toolchain and CLI-output-is-not-structured-logging rationale.

rounds.question: `reset-db` drops the settings_revisions table it just validated as authoritative, then the plan lets YAML govern restart only for a 'genuinely fresh' home — so restart either fails after destruction or silently promotes stale YAML. Also, the reset-in-progress marker's remediation ('rerun the same command') could loop forever if the same failure recurs. How should recovery work?
options: Both variants discard the latest revision

rounds.question: The plan writes GANTRY_CONTROL_HOST/GANTRY_CONTROL_PORT into .env, but decision 0006 reserves environment values for runtime-owned secrets and puts non-secret config in settings revisions — there's no existing bind-host/port exception.

Decision 0001 says CLI adapters must not directly mutate persistence, but the plan keeps schema reset, revision reads, and pg_stat_activity queries inside local.ts — and local.ts is already 569 lines with only 131 left under the unwaivable 700-line architecture ceiling before this safety work even lands.

The current staged diff is already 1,646 additions across eight files before the remaining destructive-safety work, and the sole task covers roughly twenty distinct proof seams — too large for one bounded task/PR.
options: Keep one task with an explicit size budget
rounds.chosen: Keep one task with an explicit size budget
